Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Fix independent-review findings on two stacked PRs in aspekts/viva, a hackathon project (HackTheBurgh, submission Sunday 12:00):
- #45: branch issue-18-decision-memory, base queue/5-skip. Opt-in saving of passed viva explanations to committed markdown in `.viva/memory/`.
- #46: branch memory-direction-check, base issue-18-decision-memory. Retrieves memory for the changed files, and a new checks/direction.md asks "is this the right direction?" when a change contradicts it.

Read AGENTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, and both PRs (`gh pr view 45`, `gh pr view 46`, and their diffs) first.

Push fix commits to the existing branches. Use normal commits, never force-push, as other branches may build on them. Fix #45 on its branch first, then merge issue-18-decision-memory into memory-direction-check and fix #46 there.

Findings to fix (GPT-6.1 Sol confirmed each with a reproduction):

1. **#45, P2: symlink validation happens after filesystem changes.** `packages/engine/src/memory/store.ts` (around line 142) recursively creates directories before validating the resolved location. With `.viva/memory` symlinked outside the repo, `nested/src` gets created outside it before the code throws. Validate every existing path component, using lstat/realpath, before creating any directory, and refuse symlinked components. Add a regression test with a nested symlink that asserts nothing is created outside the repo. Tests must work on Windows CI: skip the symlink test where symlink creation isn't permitted, with a clear skip reason.

2. **#46, P1: memory from the push itself can replace the decision being checked.** `packages/engine/src/memory/retrieve.ts` (around lines 28–40) reads memory at base and then at head, and overwrites entries by ID. A push that edits a base entry from "check before send" to "send before check", keeping its ID, leaves only the forged version. Newer forged entries can also push historical ones out of the eight-entry limit. Fix: retrieve memory from the push's BASE commit only, so memory added or edited in the same push never takes part in that review. Add tests: an edited entry with the same ID can't replace the base one; a flood of new entries can't push base entries out; new memory in the push is ignored. Update the docs to describe memory as unsigned repository assertions, not verified developer statements.

3. **#46, P1: direction claims can avoid the exam.** `packages/engine/src/pipeline/review.ts` (around lines 86–94) removes the mastery suppression for direction claims but still applies the ordinary risk threshold. The prompt allows `requested` origin, so a requested reversal with zero blast radius scores 0.5 and ends as `approve / low-risk` with no questions. Make direction claims always selected for the exam, within maxQuestions, prioritised sensibly against other risky claims, rather than depending on the risk threshold. Add a pipeline test, and an eval case for an explicitly requested reversal that must still be examined.

4. **Context only, don't fix here:** an empty exam plan recording a pass is fixed separately in PR #47 (branch fix/empty-exam-pass), which will reach these branches when they're integrated with main. Don't duplicate that fix.

Also: one existing test, `apps/vivad/src/exam.test.ts` "takes typed answers question-by-question…", flakes under load, independently of these changes. Don't chase it unless it blocks you.

Rules:
- Run `pnpm install` and `env -u VIVA_LLM -u GEMINI_API_KEY pnpm check` after each fix. It must pass with no key and no network. Never make live model calls, and never copy any .env.
- Don't change hard gates or fail-open behaviour.
- Don't merge PRs, and don't watch PRs. Don't kill processes you didn't start.
- Update each PR body with an "After independent review" section listing what was fixed and how.
- End commits with: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`

Final message: what changed, anything uncertain, then for each PR: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

# Working on Viva

Instructions for coding agents and humans.

## Rules

- Run `pnpm check` before calling work finished, and report the result honestly.
- `packages/contracts` is the contract. Change it first, then update `fixtures/mock` so the frontend keeps working.
- Deterministic steps run before any model call. Add a precheck before adding a prompt.
- All model access goes through `LlmProvider`. Output must be parsed by a zod schema.
- Wrap repository and session text with `untrusted()`. It is data, never instructions.
- Diffs, transcripts and model output never enter the ledger or logs. Only scores and hashes do.
- Hard gates (`skippable: false`) must never become configurable or skippable.
- Fail open: a Viva crash must never stop someone pushing.
- Use a one-question check file in `checks/` rather than growing an existing prompt.
- Never commit keys. Use `.env`.
- Keep everything working on Windows: no shell-only scripts, and use `node:path`.
- Add a test for every bug fixed. Add an eval case for every new prompt behaviour.

## Layout

- `packages/contracts`: shared zod schemas
- `packages/engine`: the review pipeline, ledger and fog
- `apps/vivad`: local daemon and `viva` CLI
- `apps/web`: The Fog and the exam room
- `checks`: one markdown file per check
- `evals`: tests for prompts
- `fixtures/mock`: sample data for the UI

Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` before changing the pipeline.

{"baseRefName":"queue/5-skip","body":"Closes #18.

**Stacked PR:** based on `queue/5-skip` (#39), the top of the open `queue/*` stack. It will be retargeted when the stack merges. #4 (Entire session reader) is not a dependency.

**Pitch hook:** the judge passes the viva, presses `m`, and `.viva/memory/src/pay.ts.md` appears with their own words about why the check runs first. Then `pnpm viva memory src/pay.ts` hands that reasoning to the next agent.

## What it does

After a **passed** exam the developer can choose to save their answers as project memory. Nothing happens unless they ask:

- terminal exam: `m` after the verdict
- `pnpm viva remember <reviewId>`
- `POST /v1/reviews/:id/memory`, plus `saveMemory(id)` in `apps/web/src/api/client.ts` for whoever adds a button

Viva appends a section to `.viva/memory/<path>.md` in the working tree, with the claim, the question, the explanation, and a machine-readable comment holding the location, person, date and commit. Then it prints exactly what it wrote. Nothing is shared until the developer commits the file, and deleting it forgets it.

`pnpm viva memory <file>` reads it back without the daemon and wraps the text in `untrusted()`. `AGENTS.md` now tells agents to read `.viva/memory/<path>.md` before changing a file. A later agent session finds the reasoning by path or by grep, with no Viva tooling, which meets #18's "done when".

## Why committed markdown and not a notes ref

- **Agents read files.** `src/pay.ts` → `.viva/memory/src/pay.ts.md` is findable without any Viva-specific tooling.
- **It travels with the repo.** It goes out with ordinary pushes, while `refs/notes/*` has to be pushed explicitly, and ledger notes aren't pushed automatically yet. Entire captures it with the commit, so Brain and other tools can pick it up without Viva depending on them.
- **The developer can see what's stored:** in the save output, in `git diff`, and in code review.

## Constraints kept

- **Ledger unchanged:** it still holds only scores and hashes. A test checks that `refs/notes/viva` holds no explanation text after a save.
- **Opt-in, passed answers only:** gate must be `exam-passed` (409 otherwise). Each grade must be `approve` or `endorse`, and empty answers are dropped.
- **Answers held only in daemon memory** until the developer chooses. They are never logged, and a restart forgets them (410).
- **Paths can't be steered by model output.** Memory is only written for files in the review's `git diff base...head`. `..`, absolute, backslash and `.viva/` paths are refused, and the save won't write through a symlinked memory folder.
- **Protected paths unchanged.** `.viva/memory/` doesn't trip `viva-config-changed`, and a push that also touches `.viva/config.json` or `.viva/checks/` is still a hard gate (tested).
- **Fails open.** Missing or damaged memory reads as empty, damaged sections are skipped, and a failed save in the exam shows a message without changing the verdict.
- **Windows:** `node:path` throughout, and git-style `/` paths are mapped to OS segments.
- **Contract first:** `MemoryEntry` and `SavedMemory` in `packages/contracts`, plus `fixtures/mock/memory.json`. `?mock` returns it.

## Tests

`env -u VIVA_LLM -u GEMINI_API_KEY pnpm check` passes offline: 134 tests, evals 6/6 on the mock provider.

- Engine: format round trip with awkward text, damaged entries, unsafe paths, passed-only, idempotent save, changed-files-only, symlink refusal, prechecks.
- Daemon: opt-in, 409/404/410, ledger stays clean.
- Ink exam: offers `m`, and a failed save keeps the verdict.
- CLI formatting, plus the web client.
- I smoke-tested `pnpm viva memory` by hand against a temp repo, which caught and fixed a macOS `/var` → `/private/var` path bug.

## Not verified

- No live model run; everything used the mock provider.
- Windows console not exercised by hand; the symlink test is skipped on Windows.
- No web UI button yet: the screens belong to Kay and Sophina.

{"baseRefName":"issue-18-decision-memory","body":"Stretch goal: a memory layer for "is this the right direction?" questions.

**Stacked PR:** based on `issue-18-decision-memory` (#45), which is based on `queue/5-skip` (#39). It will be retargeted when the stack merges. It doesn't depend on #4.

**Pitch hook:** the developer saves "the check runs before the charge on purpose". Later an agent quietly reorders it, and `git push` asks: *"You told us checking the card before sending it was deliberate; this change reverses it. Is that the right direction, and why?"* A push touching files with no memory costs zero extra tokens.

## How it works

1. **Deterministic retrieval, before any model call** (`packages/engine/src/memory/retrieve.ts`). One `git ls-tree` per end of the push, then `git show` only for `.viva/memory/<file>.md` of changed files.
   - It reads **base and head**: base so a change can't hide the decision it reverses by editing that decision's memory, and head for memory committed in the same push.
   - It drops entries that match the injection patterns, and entries filed under another path. It keeps at most 8.
2. **One new check file, `checks/direction.md`**, which declares `needs: memory` in its frontmatter (`parseCheck` rejects unknown values).
   - `runChecks` skips it with **no model call** when nothing relevant is recorded, and only this check receives the memory, inside `untrusted("memory", …)`. No existing prompt grew.
3. **Output is the existing zod `CheckResult`**, so contradictions become ordinary ranked claims and then exam questions.
   - Direction claims ignore mastery: knowing the code doesn't settle whether reversing a recorded decision is intended.
   - If the intent explicitly asks for the reversal, the claim is `requested` and usually ranks under the threshold.
4. **Fails open.** Any error reading memory means an empty memory list, so the review carries on as before.

## Evals (mock provider, offline)

| Case | Want | Got |
|---|---|---|
| reverses a recorded decision | exam (direction), 5 calls | exam (direction), 5 calls |
| consistent with a recorded decision | low-risk, 4 calls | low-risk, 4 calls |
| same reversal with no memory | low-risk, 3 calls | low-risk, 3 calls |

The original six cases keep their token counts, so the check costs nothing where there's no memory. The mock flags a memory as reversed when the diff removes a line it covers. That proves retrieval, wiring and token use, **not** model judgement.

## Tests

`env -u VIVA_LLM -u GEMINI_API_KEY pnpm check` passes offline: 144 tests, evals 9/9. `retrieve.test.ts` covers:

- changed-files-only retrieval
- emptied memory still found at base, and memory added in the push found at head
- poisoned and misfiled entries dropped
- damaged memory and a missing repo
- no call without memory, and memory sent as untrusted to the direction check only
- end-to-end question wording
- the consistent change stays quiet
- mastery ignored for direction claims
- fail open when the reader throws

## Not verified / notes

- **No live Gemini run.** The prompt's real precision is unmeasured. Run `pnpm evals` with a real provider before the demo.
- The planner prompt is unchanged. With Gemini the question wording comes from the claim summary format in `checks/direction.md`, not a fixed template.
- In one of three full `pnpm check` runs, the existing exam test "takes typed answers question-by-question…" failed with an Ink input timing flake under load. It passed alone 3/3 and in the other two full runs. It's not related to this change, but I'm flagging it.
- Merging main later: `evals/run.ts` changed there (#3 and #4). This PR's eval lives in new files (`evals/direction.ts`, `evals/cases/direction.ts`), so the conflict is a one-line call in `run.ts`. `review.ts` and `checks.ts` will need small hand merges with #4's session budget.

# Architecture

Viva reviews the human, not the code. It deliberately follows the same design as Mabel, the PR engine G-Research described in their workshop, so that it feels familiar to engineers who run this kind of system.

| Mabel | Viva |
|---|---|
| Reviews whether the code is right | Reviews whether a person understands it |
| GitHub PR, Kafka, review service, Kubernetes job, Python harness | `git push`, pre-push hook, local daemon, engine |
| One question per check, in markdown | Same, in `checks/` |
| Verdicts: reject, defer, approve, endorse | Same |
| Aggregate: worst wins | Same, across graded answers |
| Deterministic checks before any LLM call | Same, so many pushes cost no tokens |
| Prompt injection scan defers | Same, and it is a hard gate |
| Some gates can't be disabled by config | `skippable: false` gates |
| Changes to its own config need a human | `.viva/config.json` and `.viva/checks/` are protected |
| Findings stay in the job. Only verdict, counts and status leave | Diffs and transcripts stay in the review. Only scores and hashes reach the ledger |
| Evals: tests for prompts, graded on finding bugs and not flagging clean changes | `evals/`, same grading |

## The review

```
git push
  -> pre-push hook -> vivad
  -> collect the diff and session context
  -> deterministic prechecks       docs only, too large, protected paths
  -> injection scan                match: defer, cannot be skipped
  -> checks, in parallel           one question each, schema-enforced
  -> risk ranking                  plain arithmetic, no model
  -> plan up to 3 questions
  -> exam                          voice or typed
  -> grade                         separate model, transcript and rubric only
  -> aggregate, worst wins
  -> ledger -> verdict -> hook
```

Each step stops the review if it can decide, so the cheapest step wins.

## Push contexts and retries

The CLI uses an Ink typed exam when output is attached to a real terminal and no known agent/CI marker is present. Its input comes from the controlling terminal, not the hook's stdin (which contains Git ref updates). It shows question locations, submits the complete answer set to the existing daemon API, and displays grades. Skip-with-debt requires confirmation and remains unavailable for `skippable: false` gates; the daemon also enforces this.

Without a usable terminal, the hook prints the browser exam link and exits non-zero after review creation, with instructions to finish the exam and retry the push. It does not poll. Browser auto-open is limited to likely local desktop sessions; known agents, CI and SSH sessions only receive the link. API calls have bounded timeouts. Daemon/infrastructure failures retain the fail-open policy.

The daemon deduplicates reviews by a SHA-256 identity of canonical repository path, resolved base/head commits, developer and intent. Pending exams are reused in memory. Completed decisions are written atomically under Git's private `viva-decisions` directory; receipts hold only the identity hash, review ID, gate status and timestamp. Both passes and failures survive daemon restart, so a failed exam cannot turn into a new low-risk approval on retry. No diff, answer, question or model prose is persisted in this cache. Pending exams are regenerated after restart; their old links expire.

`GET /v1/reviews/:id/feedback` exposes missed concepts and question locations from the in-memory review. `viva feedback <id>` formats them as untrusted data for the developer; only an explicit `--agent claude|codex` invokes an agent CLI, passing the feedback on stdin. Detailed feedback expires on daemon restart, with an explicit error; the gate decision remains. A skip leaves fog/mastery unchanged and is retained as `skipped-with-debt` in the local decision receipt.

`GET /v1/reviews/:id/code` shows the UI the lines under discussion. It serves only files in the review's commit range, from the head commit's object store rather than the working tree, and only to loopback hosts. Code stays out of logs, the ledger and decision receipts.

## Design rules

- **Fail open.** If the daemon is down, the push goes through with a warning. Reliability beats coverage, as in HRT's Blobby talk.
- **Budget per review.** `MeteredProvider` counts tokens and enforces a cap, so a bug can't burn the credits.
- **Separate grader.** The examiner converses, while the grader only sees the transcript and rubric, so accent and fluency can't affect a score.
- **Ledger in git notes.** It needs no server, travels with the repo, and leaves your branch alone. `refs/notes/viva` has to be pushed explicitly to share it.
- **Understanding expires.** Mastery halves every 14 days, and halves again when the code changes.

## Known gaps

- entire-graph is a stub, and blast radius uses `git grep`.
- The Entire session reader only sees checkpoints in local git refs. Commits linked after the fact with `entire session attach`, and checkpoints stored in another repo, return no session. Subagent transcripts are not read.
- A push mixing agent and hand-written commits gets context for the agent commits only, so a hand-written change can look unrequested.
- Session text is fenced with `untrusted()` but the injection scan only covers the diff, so a hostile transcript relies on that fence alone.
- Traces don't exist yet. When they do, they must store stage names and token counts only, as `LlmRequest.user` holds the transcript.
- `pnpm evals` still uses the mock provider, so check quality on real diffs is unmeasured.
- The fog is per file, with blast radius at 0. Symbol-level needs entire-graph.
- Full reviews and feedback are held in memory. Only completed retry decisions survive daemon restart.
- Ledger notes aren't pushed automatically yet.
- The pipeline and terminal hook have been exercised on macOS (including a PTY with piped hook stdin). CI covers Windows, but Windows controlling-console behaviour is not yet verified; console failure falls back to the browser.

## Open problems

From G-Research's list, and worth raising with their judges:

- Callers in other repos that nobody declared.
- Asking questions of confidential design docs without leaking them.
- Determining the risk of a repo with this system enabled.

Completed decisions are written atomically under Git's private `viva-decisions` directory; receipts hold only the identity hash, review ID, gate status and timestamp. Both passes and failures survive daemon restart, so a failed exam cannot turn into a new low-risk approval on retry. No diff, answer, question or model prose is persisted in this cache. Pending exams are regenerated after restart; their old links expire.

Detailed feedback expires on daemon restart, with an explicit error; the gate decision remains. result.output:
### Questioning the direction

Saved memory is used to question later changes that cut across it. Memory is an unsigned assertion in the repository, not a verified statement by a developer: anyone who can commit can write a section in anyone's name. So, before any model call, the review reads the memory for the changed files from git at the push's base commit only. Memory that the push itself adds or edits never takes part in reviewing that push. A change can't rewrite the decision it reverses, push older decisions out with a flood of new entries, or plant memory to steer its own review. New memory only counts once it is in a later push's base. Entries that look like instructions to the reviewer, or are filed under another path, are dropped, and at most 8 are kept.

`checks/direction.md` declares `needs: memory`. With no relevant memory it is skipped without a model call, so pushes elsewhere cost no extra tokens. Otherwise it alone receives the memory, inside `untrusted()`, and returns ordinary `CheckResult` claims, such as "You told us X was deliberate; this change reverses it". These are ranked like any claim, but always reach the exam, whatever their risk score. Neither knowing the code nor having asked for the change settles whether reversing a recorded decision is the right direction, so these claims ignore the developer's mastery and the risk threshold. An intent that explicitly asks for the reversal makes the claim `requested`, which lowers its score but not its place. Reversals come first in the exam, and remaining questions go to the riskiest other claims, up to the usual 3. Reading memory can't block a push: any failure means no memory.

It is separate from the ledger, which still holds only scores and hashes. `.viva/memory/` is not a protected path, so saving memory doesn't trip `viva-config-changed`, and a push that also touches `.viva/config.json` or `.viva/checks/` is still a hard gate. Missing or damaged memory reads as empty, and a failed save never changes a verdict.

input.command:
git status --short; git add -A && git commit -q -m "Judge a push only by memory already in its base, and always examine reversals

Memory was read at both base and head and merged by ID, so a push could
rewrite the decision it reversed, keeping its ID, or flood older entries
out of the eight-entry limit. It is now read at the push's base only:
memory is an unsigned repository assertion, and memory the push adds or
edits never takes part in reviewing that push.

Direction claims ignored mastery but still had to clear the risk
threshold, so a requested reversal with no blast radius scored 0.5 and
was approved as low-risk with no questions. They are now ranked first
and always selected for the exam, within maxQuestions, with the
remaining questions going to the riskiest other claims.
